solutions.task: Identify experimental evidence supporting particle-like energy exchange by light.
solutions.independent_solution: In the ordinary single-photon photoelectric regime, a material has a threshold frequency; increasing intensity below threshold does not produce the ordinary external photoelectric emission. Above threshold, maximum kinetic energy increases with frequency rather than intensity. These observations support discrete energy transfer E=h nu. Radiation pressure demonstrates momentum transfer but is not, by itself, a unique proof of a photon description because classical electromagnetic waves also exert pressure.
solutions.distinction: Frequency changes the energy per photon; intensity at fixed frequency changes the incident photon rate.

solutions.independent_solution: For work function A, the ideal threshold is nu0=A/h. In the emitting regime Kmax=h nu-A; for fixed material and frequency Kmax does not increase with intensity. At fixed frequency above threshold, saturation photocurrent increases approximately in proportion to intensity when collection and response remain linear. Emission has no measurable accumulation delay on the time scales of the ordinary experiment. These laws apply to the usual single-photon regime, not intense-field multiphoton effects.
solutions.distinction: Separate emission threshold, maximum energy, electron emission rate and emission delay.

solutions.task: State the Planck constant with units.
solutions.independent_solution: The exact SI value is h=6.62607015 times 10^-34 J s, equivalently J/Hz. The historical approximation 6.6 times 10^-34 J s is consistent to two significant figures. An erg is 10^-7 J, so the corresponding cgs value is 6.62607015 times 10^-27 erg s, not joule-seconds.
solutions.distinction: Preserve the numerical exponent and distinguish energy-time from energy-per-time units.

solutions.task: Derive photon energy, mass convention and momentum from frequency.
solutions.independent_solution: For a free photon in vacuum, E=h nu and p=E/c=h nu/c. Its invariant rest mass is m0=0. Under the source's historical energy-equivalent convention, meq=E/c^2=h nu/c^2; this quantity is not a nonzero rest mass. The source's mass wording must not silently replace the modern invariant-mass convention.
solutions.distinction: Energy, momentum, invariant rest mass and historical energy-equivalent mass are different quantities.

solutions.task: Compare radiation pressure on a mirror and a black surface.
solutions.independent_solution: At equal incident intensity I and normal incidence, incident radiation contributes pressure I/c to a perfect absorber and 2I/c to a perfect reflector. Reflection reverses photon momentum so the normal momentum transfer is doubled. Compare only this incident-light pressure, not additional thermal recoil or different intensities.
solutions.distinction: Absorption removes the incident normal momentum; ideal reflection reverses it.
